Yes. The standard diagnostic is $70 (reduced from $89) and the commercial diagnostic is $119 (reduced from $149). Both are credited toward the repair if you go ahead. We give you the repair price before any work starts, so you can decide with the number in front of you.

The diagnostic is a single on-site visit fee. The standard visit is $70 and the commercial visit is $119; both cover testing and a written diagnosis, and the full fee is credited toward the repair if you approve the work.

The range is an approximate estimate that covers the common parts and labor for that appliance. The exact price depends on the failed component and access; we confirm it on site after the diagnostic, before any work starts.

No. The diagnostic is the only visit fee. There is no separate trip charge, and the repair range already includes parts and labor.

Only if the diagnosis changes once the appliance is opened, and you approve the new number first. The invoice never includes work you did not agree to.

No. The same published ranges apply Monday through Saturday, 7 AM to 7 PM. Emergency commercial call-outs are quoted before dispatch.

We tell you before you spend more on it. The diagnostic still applies, and you keep the written diagnosis and the part price.

Every appliance has a published approximate range that covers parts and labor. The technician confirms the exact price on site after the diagnostic, before work starts; the full table is on the pricing page.

Same-day visits are usual when you call before noon across all four service zones. If a part has to be ordered, you get the ETA before we leave, and we schedule the return visit at that price.

Call (619) 555-0142 or use the booking form: name, phone, ZIP and appliance. We call back within 15 minutes during business hours with a two-hour arrival window.

The appliance type and brand, plus the model and serial numbers from the plate — inside the refrigerator cabinet, behind the dryer door, under the cooktop. It lets us check the parts diagram before the visit, so the van leaves with the right part.

Usually. Common start components, fans, thermistors and valves ride on the van. If a part has to be ordered, you get the price and the ETA before we leave, and the return visit is scheduled at that price.

You get the part price and the ETA before we leave, and the return visit is scheduled at the same approved price. If the appliance is beyond economical repair, we tell you first.

Yes. The technician needs access to the appliance and to the water or gas shut-off where it applies, and the invoice is signed at the address.

Most diagnostics take 20 to 30 minutes. A repair is usually finished in the same visit; sealed-system work and backordered parts can need a return appointment, booked at the price you approved.

Parts and labor are covered for 90 days. The warranty is written on the invoice, not just on this page, and it applies to the specific repair we performed.

Factory parts are matched to the model and serial before anything is ordered. Where a factory part is backordered, you get the part number, the price and the ETA before we leave.

Start components, thermistors, fans, water inlet valves, door gaskets and the common heater kits. Anything else is ordered by part number once the diagnosis is confirmed.

You get the part number, the price and the ETA in writing before we leave, and the return visit is booked at the price you approved.

Yes. Fix Spark is BEAR licensed and carries liability insurance. Every repair carries a 90-day parts and labor warranty, printed on the invoice.

Yes. You keep the written diagnosis with the part number and the price, whether or not you go ahead with the repair.

Major residential brands including Sub-Zero, Wolf, Thermador, Viking, Miele, Gaggenau, KitchenAid, LG, Samsung, Whirlpool, GE and Bosch, plus commercial kitchen equipment. If we cannot source the part, we tell you on the first visit rather than leave you waiting.

Refrigerators, freezers, ice makers, washers, dryers, ovens, stoves and cooktops, dishwashers and commercial kitchen equipment. Nine categories, one diagnostic fee.

Yes. We work on 500-series, 600-series, Designer and PRO built-ins, plus undercounter and outdoor refrigeration. Read the model and serial from the plate inside the cabinet when you call.

Yes. Wine storage is on the same refrigeration range, about $149 to $420 as an estimate. Temperature, evaporator fan and condenser airflow are tested before the quote, and the exact price is confirmed on site.

A failed compressor is diagnosed with pressures and current draw. The replacement is quoted with parts and labor, and the 90-day warranty is written on the invoice.

Sometimes not. If the unit is beyond economical repair, we say so before you spend more on it. The diagnostic still applies, and you keep the written diagnosis.

Wolf, Thermador, Viking, Miele, Gaggenau, Dacor, JennAir, Bertazzoni, BlueStar, Monogram and DCS are on the brand list. Factory parts are matched to the model and serial before anything is ordered.

North County, Central San Diego, East County and South Bay. Same-day visits are usual when you call before noon; the callback comes within 15 minutes during business hours.

Monday through Saturday, 7 AM to 7 PM. The line is answered by a person during those hours, and the callback comes within 15 minutes.

No. The diagnostic is the only visit fee, and it is the same across the four service zones.

Yes. Fix Spark is locally owned and works only in San Diego County; the owner runs the same schedule as the crew.

Cafes, offices, salons, short-term rentals and property managers. Priority scheduling, one invoice per property, and the same licensed technicians as residential work.

Yes — prep refrigerators, commercial dishwashers, ice machines and cooking lines. Commercial call-outs are quoted after a site visit; the $119 commercial diagnostic (reduced from $149) applies and is credited toward the repair.

Yes. Commercial accounts get priority scheduling, and emergency call-outs are quoted before dispatch so the price is agreed before a technician is sent.

Yes. Property managers get one invoice per property, with each visit itemized by appliance and the approved price attached.
